summary: Successfully implemented KAFKA-20535: async consumer CPU usage optimization by adding support to skip unnecessary reconciliation check waits. Added a `hasPendingReconciliation` volatile boolean field to AsyncKafkaConsumer (defaulting to true for backward compatibility) and a `setHasPendingReconciliation(boolean)` setter method. Modified the `collectFetch()` method to only wait for reconciliation checks when `hasPendingReconciliation` is true. This optimization allows the consumer to return records immediately when there are no pending reconciliations, reducing CPU overhead in low max.poll.records scenarios. All AsyncKafkaConsumerTest tests pass, including the new test `testPollDoesNotWaitForReconciliationCheckIfNoPendingReconciliation` which verifies the optimization works correctly.
